title: eval-harness: per-prompt regression CI hook + quality gating for model onboarding
author: Claire Kim
release_notes: Add per-prompt regression CI hook and configurable quality gating for model onboarding. New CI job evaluates candidate model outputs against canonical prompt sets and fails the gate on statistically significant regressions. Includes dashboarding hooks and documentation for onboarding. Backward compatible by default; opt-in gating for existing pipelines.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed several subtle regressions during recent model rollouts where aggregate eval metrics looked OK but a small number of customer-facing prompts regressed substantially. This PR adds a per-prompt regression CI hook and a configurable quality gate so model onboarding and PRs that touch inference behavior get blocked when important prompt-level regressions occur.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces eval-harness/hooks/per_prompt_gate.py: a lightweight CI hook that runs the eval harness on a curated prompt set and computes per-prompt deltas against a saved baseline. Uses bootstrap confidence intervals to detect regressions.
- Adds eval-ci job in ci/configs/eval-ci.yml that can run on PRs touching inference/runtime/model interfaces or on model onboarding branches. Job supports partial run (changed prompts only) to keep runtime sane.
- Adds prompt_metrics helper and new metrics tags so the Console can surface per-prompt regressions in the rollout dashboard.
- Provides documentation and onboarding notes: docs/eval-harness/quality-gates.md and examples/onboarding/README.md.
- Tests: tests/eval/test_prompts_regression.py with synthetic baseline and mock runner to validate detection logic and false positive rate.

Commits (summary):
- 3a7e1b2: initial per_prompt_gate implementation + unit tests
- 8c4f2d0: integrate bootstrap CI thresholds + config wiring
- d9b7a11: ci: add eval-ci job and runner script
- b2e6f4c: docs and examples, update console wiring
- f1c3a9e: fix edge cases for empty predictions + add retries in runner

Changed areas (high level snippets):
- eval-harness/hooks/per_prompt_gate.py: core hook. Key function: run_and_compare(model, prompt_set, baseline_path, threshold_config). Uses 2k bootstrap samples by default; configurable via env var.
- ci/configs/eval-ci.yml: new job eval-per-prompt that runs only when paths match and is skippable with [skip eval].
- docs/eval-harness/quality-gates.md: onboarding instructions and recommended prompt set curation guidelines.

Testing and CI notes:
- Local dev script scripts/dev/run_local_eval.sh spins up a lightweight runner using the same container image the CI uses.
- CI initially failed due to an intermittent network call in the integration runner. I added retries and a short cache for baseline artifacts; CI re-run passed (see status).
- We intentionally made the gate opt-in in the onboarding flow; the default CI job will not block teams until they add the gate config to their model registry entry.

Telemetry and observability:
- prompt_metrics exports per-prompt delta, p-value, and confidence interval to metrics backend. The Console component GatesStatus.tsx renders a sortable table of the top regressions and links back to prompt examples.

Performance and cost considerations:
- The hook supports limiting max prompts per run and partial-run mode that only evaluates changed prompts. We included intelligent sampling for long prompt sets to keep cost bounded. 

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (done).
2) Add gates to internal onboarding pipelines and monitor for 2 weeks.
3) Recommend teams add opt-in gate to their model registry entries; gradually make it a default for high-risk models.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] CI job added and green after retry
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Console wiring added
- [x] Telemetry metrics instrumented

Review conversation (high level):
- Devon Mills (2025-11-21): "Can we avoid running the full prompt set on every PR? Concerned about cost for large prompt libraries."
  - Claire: "Addressed — added partial-run mode and sampling; caller can configure max_prompts and mode in default_gates.yaml."
- Jordan Lee (2025-11-22): "What false positive rate are we targeting? Also ensure statistical test is robust under ties."
  - Claire: "We target ~1% FPR by default using bootstrap with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple prompts. Ties handled by small jitter in scorer; added tests to validate behavior."
- Priya Rao (2025-11-24): "Please add docs for how to interpret gate failures in the Console and suggested remediation steps."
  - Claire: "Done — added section with example remediation steps and rollback guidance."
- Devon Mills (approval, 2025-11-25): "Approving after CI stability fixes. Please monitor noise in first week."

Merge outcome: Squash and merge on 2025-11-27 after final CI green. Post-merge actions: uploaded baseline artifact to S3 (internal path documented) and created a Linear task ENG-5480 to monitor gate noise for first 2 weeks.

Notes for maintainers:
- Config file eval-harness/config/default_gates.yaml contains safe defaults that err on avoiding false positives. Teams can tighten thresholds during onboarding.
- If you hit flaky CI due to network timeouts fetching baselines, set EVAL_BASELINE_CACHE_SECONDS to a higher value in CI environment.

If there are follow-ups I'd like to prioritize: auto-suggest remediation prompts in Console and a small tutorial notebook for teams to build a minimal prompt set for gating.
